Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In these appeals, the Insurance Company is challenging the common judgment dated 04.06.2015
passed in MVC.No.786/2013 and Mvc No.787/2013 by the Xii Additional Small Cause Judge and
Member, Mact, Bengaluru (Scch - 8) (in short 'the Tribunal').

In the cross objection, the
petitioners are seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per their ranking before the
Tribunal.

Sri. Thimma Reddy (Died) vs The Manager on 11 September, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70997621/
5

3.

Brief facts of the case are, one Sri.Anjaneyalu, the deceased, the son of the petitioners and 3rd
respondent in Mvc No.786/2013, (in short the deceased), while riding the motor cycle bearing
Registration No.KA-01-R-8358 along with the petitioner in Mvc No.787/2013 from Dodda
Kannahalli to Sarjapura road, while crossing the signal in Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 front of Wood Line
Apartment a car bearing Reg.No.KL-07- Bd-5770 came from the opposite direction and dashed
against the motorcycle, due to which both the riders fell down sustained injuries.

In spite of the
deceased treated at Venkateshwara hospital and also at D.G Hospital, Bengaluru, on 24.10.2012 he
was succumbed to death.

The petitioners being the parents of the deceased and the injured pillion
rider have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- and
Rs.10,00,000/- respectively in their claim petitions.
4. The claim was opposed by the owner and insurer of the car as well as the motorcycle in the
respective
cases .

The Tribunal has taken the common evidence in both the cases and after hearing
both the parties by impugned common judgment allowed both the claim petitions against the
respondent Nos.1 and 2 and awarded compensation of Rs.10,55,051/- in respect of the parents of the
deceased and Rs.1,15,760/- in respect of the injured pillion rider.
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095
5.
In Mvc No.787/2013 claim against the owner and insurer of the motorcycle is dismissed.

Aggrieved by the same Insurance Company of the car is before this Court whereas the petitioners in
Mvc No.786/2013 seeking enhancement have filed the cross objection.
6.

Heard the argument of Sri.H.S.Lingaraju., learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the car,
Sri.R.L Uday Kumar., learned counsel appearing for the 2nd petitioner in Mvc No.786/2013 and
Sri.K.Suresh, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company of the motor cycle.

7. Sri. H.S.Lingaraju has contended that, there was a road maiden on the middle of the road, it is a
one way traffic but the motorcycle came from the wrong direction and all of a sudden without
observing the incoming traffic taken turn, without giving any signal and tailored the accident.

It was
due to complete negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

But the Tribunal ignored the same
and fastened the complete negligence against the driver of Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 the car.

Police
investigation culminated in filing joint charge sheet against the driver of the car, as well as the
deceased.

It is also contended that the compensation awarded under the conventional heads is
disproportionate and the same is on the higher side.

It is further contended that the rate of interest
at 8% awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side, no banks will offer interest at higher rates, the
Tribunal has not recorded any reason for awarding higher rate of interest and it has to be reduced to
6%.
8.

Learned counsel for the cross objector has contended that the accident is of the year 2012, the
deceased was working as a courier boy, earning Rs.8,000/- per month.

Tribunal has taken the
income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-, even if notional income is considered it will be not less than
Rs.7,000/-, future prospects of 40% is also not considered and he sought for enhancement of
compensation.

Sri. Thimma Reddy (Died) vs The Manager on 11 September, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70997621/
6

- 10 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095
9.

As regards negligence on the part of the deceased is concerned, it is contended that the deceased
at the time of accident was crossing the road to go to other side with due care.

The impact of the
accident is so much, that the driver of the car was under an uncontrollable speed.

If he was under a
controllable speed within the limits of City, such an accident would not have been occurred.

The
Tribunal has analyzed in detail the material placed before it and came to a satisfactory conclusion,
that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and fastened the liability
against the car.
As the petitioners are getting the compensation 10 years after the accident.

Rate of
interest at 8% awarded is just and proper.

10. It is contended by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the motor cycle that the
Tribunal considering the material on record came to the right conclusion that, the complete
negligence

was on the part of the driver of the car, there was no negligence on the part of the
deceased and rightly dismissed the claim
- 11 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 against the owner and insurer of the motor cycle and he has supported the
impugned judgment.

11. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for
both parties and perused the records.

12. The following points arise for consideration:
i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded the just compensation ?
ii) Whether the Tribunal is right in awarding the interest at 8% ?
iii) Whether the Tribunal is right in Attributing complete negligence on the part of
the driver of the car ?
Re point No.(i);
13.
The deceased was aged 27 years as pointed out in the prosecution papers.

A person with no proof
of income will earn not less than Rs.7,000/- per month in the year 2012.

Though the petitioners
claim that the deceased was a courier boy, the employer is not examined before
- 12 -
Sri. Thimma Reddy (Died) vs The Manager on 11 September, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70997621/
7

Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has considered the notional income of the
deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.

The deceased was married to the 3rd respondent Smt. Bharathi
she has not joined the in-laws in the claim petition.

Since there are three dependents 1/3rd has to be
deducted towards personal expenses and future prospects of 40% has to be considered and the
applicable multiplier is '17'.

Then the loss of dependency will be Rs.7000+2800 (40%)= 9800-3266
(1/3rd)=Rs.6534 x 12 x 17 = 13,32,936.

Towards conventional heads, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each is
awarded to the wife as loss of consortium, parental consortium and Rs.15,000/- each Towards loss
of estate and funeral expenses.

14. In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance
Company Ltd V/S Pranay Sethi And Ors., reported in (2017)16 Scc 680, 10% has to be
given in appreciation under the conventional heads as the accident is 12 years
- 13 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 old.

National Insurance
Company Ltd V/S Pranay Sethi And Ors., reported in (2017)16 Scc 680

sentences.text:
Accordingly, compensation under conventional heads comes to
Rs.1,65,000/-.
15.

The deceased was treated in two hospitals and the petitioners have spent Rs.64,051/- towards
treatment.
The same is ordered to be reimbursed by the Tribunal and it is kept intact.

If all is put
together total compensation comes to Rs.15,61,987/- instead of Rs.10,55,051/- awarded by the
Tribunal thereby enhancement of Rs.5,06,936/-.

It is the just compensation that the petitioners and
the 3rd respondent are entitled to under the facts and circumstances of the case.

Accordingly point
No.(i) is answered.

Re point No.(ii);
16.
As regarding rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded 8% interest.

On perusal of
the impugned judgment, no special reasons are assigned by the Tribunal.

Interest at higher rate is
permissible in cases where the special reasons are to be recorded.

The Tribunal did not answered
any reasons why the interest of 8% per
- 14 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 annum was awarded.

Under such circumstances, it is relevant to refer to the
judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and
Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (Mv) disposed of on
24.08.2020 wherein with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of
Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid
down principles regarding award of interest, which reads thus:
"52.

Thus, under Section 34 of Cpc being squarely applicable to the interest awarded
by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite
interest and discretion being vested with the Court/Tribunal to award interest from
Sri. Thimma Reddy (Died) vs The Manager on 11 September, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70997621/
8

the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not
exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the
Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted. . . . . . . . ."

In view of the law laid down, without reasons higher rate of interest is not permissible and therefore
the petitioners
- 15 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 are entitled to interest at 6% p.a.
Point No.(ii) is answered accordingly.

Re point No.(iii);
17.

As regards the contributory negligence is concerned, no doubt the accident has taken place on
one way road.

The road having a maiden and the motorcycle came to the right side of the road on
the complete border.

All of a sudden from the border of the road, the riders attempted to cross the
road to go to the other side.

At that time, the car which was on the higher speed came and dashed on
the right hind portion of the motorcycle and the impact damaged the back side of the motor cycle.

This clearly goes to show that when the motorists were crossing the road they must be very careful
and should have watched the incoming traffic before attempting to cross the road.

But at the same
time, it is not a license for the incoming car to hit against a person who is violating the road rules.

Hence, having regard to the circumstances and the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased as
- 16 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 well as the injured and the damaged to the motor cycle clearly point out
major negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

Hence, it is persuasive that 25% to be
attributed against the deceased as contributory negligence and that of the driver of the car at 75%.

18. The Tribunal has dismissed the claim against the owner and the Insurance Company of the
motor cycle.

In view of 25% of contributory negligence attributed against the deceased who was the
rider of the motor cycle, the owner and Insurance Company of the motor cycle has to pay 25% of the
compensation to the injured pillion rider and 75% has to be paid by the Insurance Company of the
car.
Accordingly, point No.(iii) is answered.

19. In view of finding on point No.(i) to (iii) the Order of dismissal of the claim against the owner
and Insurance Company of the motor cycle in respect of the injured petitioner is liable to be
set-aside, accordingly appeal filed by the Insurance Company of the car and cross objection
- 17 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 filed by the 2nd petitioner merits consideration, in the result, the following;
Order
Sri. Thimma Reddy (Died) vs The Manager on 11 September, 2024

9

i) Both the appeals as well as the cross objection is partly allowed;
ii) The imp
ugned judgment and award is hereby modified;
iii) The Order of dismissal of the claim petition against the respondent Nos.3 and 4 in MVC No.787/2013 is hereby set aside.

iv) The petitioners and the 3rd respondent in MVC No.786/2013, are entitled to 75% out of total compensation of Rs.15,61,987/- i.e., Rs.11,71,490/- from the insurer of the car.
v) The petitioner in MVC No.787/2013 is entitled to 75% and 25% out of total of Rs.1,19,760/- from the insurer of the car and motorcycle respectively.
vi) The petitioners in both claim petitions are entitle to the interest at 6% per annum on - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:37095 the compensation from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
vii) Since the 1st petitioner is no more, the apportionment shall be made equally between the 2nd petitioner and the 3rd respondent in MVC No.786/2013.
viii) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
ix) Both the Insurance Company shall deposit their share of compensation with interest supra within eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
x) The 2nd petitioner and the 3rd respondent in  MVC No.786/2013 are not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for 1304 days, in filing of cross objection belatedly.

SD/-

opennyai_summary.issue:
12. The following points arise for consideration:
i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded the just compensation ?
ii) Whether the Tribunal is right in awarding the interest at 8% ?
iii) Whether the Tribunal is right in Attributing complete negligence on the part of
the driver of the car ?
Re point No.(i);
13.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the just compensation that the petitioners and
the 3rd respondent are entitled to under the facts and circumstances of the case.
As regarding rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded 8% interest.
On perusal of
the impugned judgment, no special reasons are assigned by the Tribunal.
Interest at higher rate is
permissible in cases where the special reasons are to be recorded.
Under such circumstances, it is relevant to refer to the
judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and
Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (Mv) disposed of on
24.08.2020 wherein with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of
Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid
down principles regarding award of interest, which reads thus:
"52.
The road having a maiden and the motorcycle came to the right side of the road on
the complete border.
All of a sudden from the border of the road, the riders attempted to cross the
road to go to the other side.
At that time, the car which was on the higher speed came and dashed on
the right hind portion of the motorcycle and the impact damaged the back side of the motor cycle.
This clearly goes to show that when the motorists were crossing the road they must be very careful
and should have watched the incoming traffic before attempting to cross the road.
But at the same
time, it is not a license for the incoming car to hit against a person who is violating the road rules.
Hence, having regard to the circumstances and the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased as
- 16 -
Nc: 2024:Khc:37095 well as the injured and the damaged to the motor cycle clearly point out
major negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
Hence, it is persuasive that 25% to be
attributed against the deceased as contributory negligence and that of the driver of the car at 75%.
18. The Tribunal has dismissed the claim against the owner and the Insurance Company of the
motor cycle.
In view of 25% of contributory negligence attributed against the deceased who was the
rider of the motor cycle, the owner and Insurance Company of the motor cycle has to pay 25% of the
compensation to the injured pillion rider and 75% has to be paid by the Insurance Company of the
car.
